core_obligations: Show that the functor is an fppf sheaf, using that an fppf covering is surjective on underlying sets (proof lines 3189-3193).

Choose an etale covering of the space by affine schemes, note that the base changes of the functor along the members are etale over it and jointly surjective onto it, and reduce to the affine case (proof lines 3195-3202).

In the affine case, identify a point of the base changed functor as a morphism into the affine member whose image lies in the inverse image of the closed subset, and conclude by the statement on completions of affine schemes (proof lines 3202-3207).
proof_roadmap: Covering reduction to the affine case (proof lines 3195-3202).
difficulty_reason: For an algebraic space X over a scheme and a closed subset T of its underlying space, the lemma asserts that the functor of morphisms into X whose image lies in T is a formal algebraic space (statement lines 3178-3187). The proof first checks the sheaf condition: an fppf covering induces a surjection on underlying sets, so the condition that the image lies in a fixed closed subset is local, and since the space is an fppf sheaf the functor is one as well (proof lines 3189-3193). It then chooses an etale covering of the space by affine schemes, observes that the base changes of the functor along the members of that covering are etale over it and jointly surjective onto it, and reduces to the case of an affine scheme (proof lines 3195-3202). In that case a point of the base changed functor is a morphism into the affine member whose image lies in the inverse image of the closed subset, so the assertion is exactly the statement that the completion of an affine scheme along a closed subset is an affine formal algebraic space (proof lines 3202-3207). The claim is H2: the sheaf condition and the covering reduction are carried out explicitly, and the affine case is a named statement which is applied after identifying the base changed functor.
